blueprint_sources: Berkeley Hills split-level on steep grade — pier-and-grade-beam foundation, stepped living levels
Oakland Hills fire-rebuild reference (post-1991) — WUI construction, stepped massing on 25% slope
Marin County hillside contemporary — multiple rooflines, integrated decks at each level

petronus_classification.note: Hillside stepped homes are defined by their split-level relationship to steep terrain. WUI fire zone requirements drive facade and vent material choices. Multi-zone HVAC is mandatory given large vertical separations between levels.

lot.note: Steeply sloped lot — grade relationship between street, main entry, and rear yard varies. Confirm street level vs. sewer main elevation before placing bathrooms.

structure.soft_story_note: Hillside homes with open lower-level parking or unbraced cripple walls under stepped lower floors are high soft-story risk. Mandatory shear wall design at all levels.

floor_program.note: Program is distributed across multiple half-levels stepping down the slope. Street-entry level is typically mid-house. Living areas and bedrooms cascade up or down from entry.

street_level.mep_note: Panel typically lands here closest to utility pole/vault. EV charging in garage. Establish reference grade for sewer main relationship check.

level_up_half.mep_note: Kitchen wet wall and main DWV stack at this level. Check if kitchen floor elevation is above or below street sewer main.

level_down_half.mep_note: CRITICAL: If any bathroom floor elevation is below the street sewer main invert, a sewage ejector pump is MANDATORY. Calculate relative elevations before specifying DWV system.

lower_level.mep_note: Ejector pump almost certainly required at this level. Route ejector discharge up to gravity drain at street-level sewer main or higher.

wet_wall.ejector_pump_note: The generator MUST compare the finished floor elevation of each bathroom to the street sewer main invert elevation. Any bathroom FFE more than 8in below sewer main invert requires a sewage ejector pump and pit — this is non-negotiable per CBC plumbing code.
wet_wall.note: Route DWV stack vertically from lowest level up through roof. Each level connects to stack via sloped branch. Ejector pump at below-grade bathrooms discharges upward to stack above sewer main elevation.

staircase.mep_note: Stairs at each half-level transition create opportunities for vertical MEP chases alongside stair stringers. Route supply, return, and vent lines in the stair wall cavity.

mep_chase.note: Stepped massing means there is no single vertical shaft from basement to roof. Each level needs its own MEP connection points. Stair wall chases are the primary vertical routing spine.

hvac.reason: Large vertical separation between levels and different sun/wind exposure at each level creates distinct thermal zones. A single air handler cannot properly condition all levels.
hvac.outdoor_unit_wui_note: Outdoor units must be ember-resistant if in WUI zone — specify non-combustible surrounds and clear vegetation 10ft from unit.

ejector_pump.calculation_note: Compare FFE of each bathroom to sewer main invert at property line. If FFE is <8in above sewer invert, specify ejector pump.

supply.long_run_note: Long supply runs on steep lots may require pressure-boosting — calculate static pressure loss for runs >60ft vertical.

panel.service_run_note: Utility pole or underground vault may be significantly above or below the main panel location. Calculate voltage drop for service feeder: use wire size one gauge larger than minimum if run exceeds 100ft.

solar.multiple_roof_planes_note: Stepped massing produces multiple roof levels at different elevations and orientations — optimize panel placement on south-facing planes.

massing_hints.note: Massing follows terrain contours. Each stepped level reads as a distinct volume with its own roofline. Decks cantilever from each level to capture views. Retaining walls anchor each step to the hillside.

known_constraints_summary: EJECTOR PUMP CHECK: Compare every bathroom FFE to sewer main invert — any bathroom below sewer elevation requires ejector pump. This is a mandatory pre-design calculation.
Multi-zone HVAC required — one zone per level minimum. Single air handler cannot serve all split levels.
Voltage drop calculation required for service feeder — pole or vault may be 50-150ft from main panel, often at different elevation.
WUI zone: all exterior vents must be ember-resistant (Class A), glazing must be fire-rated, roofing must be Class A. No wood siding without fire-resistant coating.
Pier-and-grade-beam or caisson foundation on steep slopes — coordinate HVAC outdoor unit and utility service entry with foundation layout.
Soft story risk at open lower-level parking or cripple walls — seismic shear wall design required at all levels.
Seismic design category D — lateral bracing at each level is non-optional.
DWV stack must be continuous from lowest level to roof — route through stair wall chases at each half-level transition.
Multi-level supply runs may need pressure boosting for runs exceeding 60ft vertical — calculate static pressure loss.
Multiple roof planes at different elevations — optimize solar on south-facing planes only, coordinate with multi-zone HVAC condensers.
